sections.title: CLAUDE.md & Memory
points: Precedence (most to least specific): enterprise-managed policy > project CLAUDE.md (checked in, shared with the team) > user-level (~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, personal across all projects) > nested directory-level CLAUDE.md files loaded as Claude reads into that subtree.
Long or conflicting CLAUDE.md files (500+ lines, contradictory rules) degrade instruction-following — split into smaller, scoped files per subdirectory rather than one monolithic file.
Use # during a session to append a new instruction to CLAUDE.md immediately, or /memory to open and edit it directly.
Nested CLAUDE.md files let subdirectories override or add to parent conventions (e.g. a frontend/ CLAUDE.md with different lint rules than the repo root).
CLAUDE.md is prose read by the model each session, not enforced config — for hard guarantees (blocking a command, always running a formatter) use hooks or permission rules instead.
